questions.problem: What is the center and the radius of the circle with equation ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=2?$
questions.worked_solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the origin is 

$$
{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

So, the equation ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=2$ represents a circle that is centered at the origin, with radius

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{2} & =2 \\ r & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we disregarded the negative solution for the radius since the radius of a circle must be positive.

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(0,0)$ and its radius is $\sqrt{2}.$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13956996/assets/1baa0bec9c8cfdb2ce80d47e66f6ba54d34266267df3ee323a658c0f98a52f83.png)

Given that the points $X$ and $Y$ with coordinates $(1,4)$ and $(-1,-4),$ respectively, are the endpoints of a diameter of a circle centered at the origin, what is the equation of the circle?
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a circle with radius $r,$ centered at the origin, is 

$$
{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

First, we calculate the length of the diameter $\overset{―}{XY}:$
  

$$
\begin{aligned}XY & =\sqrt{{(4-(-4))}^{2}+{(1-(-1))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{8}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{68} \\  & =\sqrt{4\cdot 17} \\  & =2\sqrt{17}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\overset{―}{XY}$ is a diameter, the radius is

$$
r=\frac{XY}{2}=\frac{2\sqrt{17}}{2}=\sqrt{17}.
$$

 

So, the equation of the circle is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={(\sqrt{17})}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =17.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\sqrt{(-2-2)^{2}+{(4-(-4))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{8}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+64} \\  & =\sqrt{80} \\  & =4\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\overline{AB}$ is a diameter, the radius is

$$
r=\dfrac{AB}{2} = \dfrac {4\sqrt{5}}{2}=2\sqrt5.
$$

So, the equation of the circle is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={(2\sqrt{5})}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =20.\end{aligned}
$$
